messages:
alex_support: Customer reported that their on‑prem meter shows ~18% fewer tokens on the invoice compared to their internal audit logs for 2026-02-12 00:00–04:00 UTC. They upgraded the meter agent to v2.4.1 last night.

sam_oncall: Thanks — can you paste the exact window and any agent logs we have? Do we know which host/container ran the agent?

alex_support: Hostnames: node-12.prod.vpc, node-13.prod.vpc. Window above (00:00–04:00 UTC). Customer says heartbeat gaps around 00:13 and periodic gaps every ~7–8m. Attached their ledger summary (redacted):

```
ledger_tokens_by_minute:
  00:05: 124567
  00:12: 131220
  00:13: 0  # gap reported
  00:20: 136009
  ...
```

rachel_eng: Can we get the agent logs from node-12 for that timeframe? Also which storage backend for buffering — local disk or ephemeral tmpfs?

alex_support: They configured local disk (/var/lib/meter-buffer) with default rotate settings. Uploading the filtered agent logs (see snippet):

```
[2026-02-12T00:12:58Z] INFO  meter-agent: batch flushed (seq_start=194302, seq_end=194499) size=197
[2026-02-12T00:13:02Z] WARN  meter-agent: syscall write failed: EIO
[2026-02-12T00:13:02Z] ERROR meter-agent: failed to ack batch seq=194302..194499 -> dropped
[2026-02-12T00:13:03Z] INFO  meter-agent: heartbeat lost (last=00:06:51)
[2026-02-12T00:20:10Z] INFO  meter-agent: resumed, seq=194500
```

sam_oncall: EIO on write while flushing — that explains dropped batches. Do we also have kernel/host dmesg for the same timestamp? Could be disk flakiness.

alex_support: Customer posted dmesg: "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev sdb, sector 123456" around 00:13.

rachel_eng: OK this looks like the agent attempted to durably flush a batch, got EIO, and (pre‑2.4.2 behavior) marked the batch as dropped instead of retrying on a separate path. That would create a gap between audit log (which logs ingest before flush) and meter counts (which only count acked batches).

meter-agent-bot: recent-heartbeats: ["2026-02-12T00:06:51Z","2026-02-12T00:13:03Z","2026-02-12T00:20:10Z"]

julian_se: Two follow-ups for triage and for customer reconciliation:
1) Repro/forensics steps for Node-12:
   - Please run on node: `sudo journalctl -u meter-agent --since \"2026-02-12 00:00\" --until \"2026-02-12 04:30\" > /tmp/meter-node12.log`
   - Dump queue: `/usr/bin/meter-agent --dump-queue --out /tmp/queue-dump.json` (if the agent still has state)
   - Check buffer dir: `ls -lh /var/lib/meter-buffer` and `sudo btrfs/lsblk` (depending on FS)

2) Reconciliation suggestions for billing:
   - Use audit log deltas to compute missing seq ranges and mark as "unacked due to host I/O error" so billing can credit the customer if warranted.

maria_billing: We need the exact seq ranges + token counts to assess invoice correction. Can engineering provide a CSV with: seq_start, seq_end, token_count, reason?

rachel_eng: Will generate. Based on logs, candidate dropped range: seq=194302..194499 (~197 batches * avg tokens). We'll run `meter-tool reconcile --from 194302 --to 194499 --dump-tokens > /tmp/missing.csv` once we have access to audit store.

sam_oncall: Short term mitigation for customer: ask them to switch buffer to a different disk or NFS mount with writeback, and bump agent to v2.4.3 which has retry-on-EIO and a separate durable queue file. Also suggest increasing fsync timeout config: `durable_write_timeout_ms: 20000`

alex_support: Customer asked whether this could be clock skew-related (they saw heartbeat gaps and wondered about ntp). Any evidence?

rachel_eng: The heartbeat gaps line up with the EIO timeframe; NTP drift would cause timestamp skew but wouldn't drop batches. However we should still check system clock: `ntpq -p` and `chronyc tracking` for both nodes. If clock jumped forward, audit timestamps might misalign with ledger time windows — add to forensic checklist.

julian_se: Postmortem/action items:
- [ENG] Produce CSV for billing (seq ranges + token totals) — target 4h.
- [OPS] Confirm host disk health (smartctl) and recommend migration — target 2h.
- [ENG] Backport retry-on-EIO fix to 2.4.x stable and coordinate customer upgrade to 2.4.3 — target 24h.
- [BILLING] Prepare provisional credit template if reconciliation confirms loss — target 8h.

maria_billing: Noted. Please include an estimated token delta so we can precompute a credit.

rachel_eng: Quick estimation from sample: dropped seq range above ~194302..194499 -> approx 48k tokens (rough estimate). Will confirm.

alex_support: Customer is okay with trial mitigation (move buffer) and asked for a final postmortem when done. I'll schedule a call if they want deeper debugging.

sam_oncall: Forensics checklist posted to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-0212-metering-iowrite. Add logs and queue dumps there.

julian_se: Long term: add a reconciliation job that cross-checks audit entries vs acked seqs hourly and raises an automated ticket if mismatch > 1%. That would catch these sooner.

alex_support: Thanks all — I'll update customer in 30m with mitigation steps and our plan. :thumbsup:

maria_billing: Thanks — keep me in the loop before sending any credits.

sam_oncall: Closing loop when CSV uploaded and agent patch published.
